### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** [current main]
* **Discovered by:** local code-reviewer-standard review of PR #482 (post-merge)

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** Coverage gap

#### Expected Behavior

`tests/scripts/test-ruleset-design-invariants.sh` should detect drift in BOTH directions:
(a) live ruleset state diverges from documented design (current coverage), AND
(b) running `provision-ruleset.sh` on a clean repo would produce a different shape than current live state.

#### Actual Behavior

The test asserts (a) only. A manually-applied UI ruleset change (or a previous provisioner run with a different shape) can leave live state matching the test's expected values WHILE `provision-ruleset.sh` still emits a stale shape. A future fresh provisioner run would silently overwrite the working state.

This is Finding 1 of the 2026-05-29 DSO Review audit ("Sub-PR ruleset/review contract drift") — five inconsistent representations of how sub-PR review is enforced coexist; this test locks in only one of them.

### 3. Proposed Remediation

Part of the broader "Canonical sub-PR enforcement contract" epic:
1. Author `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/sub-pr-enforcement.md` as single source of truth
2. Rewrite `provision-ruleset.sh` to emit `required_status_checks` (current live shape) instead of stale `required_workflows`
3. Regenerate `check-ruleset-preflight.sh` "good" fixture from `provision-ruleset.sh --dry-run` so the fixture cannot drift from the provisioner
4. Add CI round-trip test: dry-run payload → preflight accepts it
5. Update `test-branch-pattern-alignment.sh` Test 4 (currently asserts `workflows` rule type — locks in wrong direction)
6. Update INSTALL.md
data.title: [provision-ruleset.sh + test-ruleset-design-invariants.sh]: provisioner output drift goes undetected -> live rulesets and provisioner shape can diverge silently
